To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the kinetics of formation of oxide-superconducting phases are determined by both the structure and dispersion of the rare-earth precursor in the oxide mixtures subjected to thermal treatment and by the temperature and oxygen partial pressure.

the rate of formation of superconductor phases from oxide mixtures subjected to thermal treatment is faster for mixtures containing Eu 2 CuO 3 as the precursor than for those containing Ho 2 CuO, La 2 CuO or Y 2 CuO.
the rate of formation of the superconductive phase is dependent on the dispersion of the precursor and that the rate is independent, or only weakly dependent, on the oxygen partial pressure at 1073K.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of formation of oxide high temperature superconductors.
the kinetics of formation of superconducting oxides, in particular the rate of formation of the oxide superconductor YBa 2 (Cu 1− y Zn y ) 3 O 6+z.
the kinetics of formation of oxide high- Tc superconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinetics of formation of oxide high Tc superconductors are not yet fully understood.
the kinetics of formation of oxide-superconductor phases is very complex.

the rate of formation of superconducting oxide is determined by a combination of factors including the structure and dispersion of the rare earth oxide precursor, the temperature, the partial pressure of oxygen and the nature of the rare earth element itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinetics of formation of the oxide superconductor phase depends on the structure of the precursor, the temperature of treatment and the partial pressure of oxygen.
the rate of formation of oxide phases is controlled by the rate of diffusion of oxygen and/or copper ions in the oxide precursor.
the kinetics of formation of the oxide superconductor is not controlled by the rate of diffusion through the solid, but by the rate of reaction of the solid with the gaseous reactants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kinetics of formation of superconducting phases is not necessarily the rate-limiting step in the processing of superconducting ceramics.
the rate of formation of the oxide superconductor is determined by the kinetics of the formation of the precursor oxide.
the rate of the formation of the 1–2–3 phase depends on the structure of the precursor.
